items.q: How do I buy a campervan in New Zealand?
items.a: Browse by location, budget and equipment, then contact the seller to arrange a viewing. Verify the vehicle identifiers and documents, check the PPSR for security interests and arrange an independent inspection before committing. The buying guide explains the handover and NZTA notification steps.

items.q: Where is the best place to buy a campervan in New Zealand?
items.a: Compare specialist marketplaces such as Kiwi Van Market, general marketplaces and local listings by city, budget and vehicle condition. Kiwi Van Market lets you browse campervans and contact sellers directly. Inspect the actual vehicle and arrange an independent inspection before paying.

items.q: Is it safe to buy a campervan from a backpacker in NZ?
items.a: A private sale requires your own checks. Meet the seller, establish their authority to sell and compare the vehicle identifiers with the documents. Use the PPSR for registered security interests and an appropriate vehicle-history report for recorded history. A marketplace listing or history link does not guarantee the vehicle’s condition.

items.q: What is a WOF (Warrant of Fitness) in New Zealand?
items.a: A WoF is a periodic vehicle safety inspection, not a mechanical pre-purchase inspection. Check the document’s expiry and current NZTA rules for the vehicle. NZTA has announced inspection changes from 1 November 2026, so an older summary of intervals may no longer apply.

items.q: What is rego (vehicle licensing) in New Zealand?
items.a: Rego usually means vehicle licensing, which is distinct from registration. Check that it is current and use NZTA’s current information for the vehicle’s fee and renewal. Registration records the person responsible for the vehicle; it is not proof of legal ownership.

items.q: What is self-contained certification in New Zealand?
items.a: Self-contained certification concerns the vehicle’s toilet, drinking water and wastewater systems. From 7 June 2026, a green warrant is required to be certified under the new requirements. Check the current certificate and warrant for the actual vehicle. Certification does not give permission to camp everywhere: local restrictions still apply.

items.q: How much does a campervan cost in New Zealand?
items.a: Compare asking prices in current listings rather than treating a fixed range as a valuation. Model, year, mileage, maintenance, conversion condition, location and certification all affect price. Kiwi Van Market’s price pages summarise advertised prices on this platform, not completed sales across New Zealand.

items.q: What is the best campervan for backpackers in NZ?
items.a: There is no single best van for every trip. Compare a Toyota Hiace, Nissan Caravan or Mazda Bongo against your budget, bed dimensions, storage, driving comfort and maintenance records. A model’s reputation cannot replace an inspection of the vehicle you plan to buy.

items.q: What should I check when inspecting a van in NZ?
items.a: Check WOF and rego dates, the plate and VIN, ownership documents, maintenance records, corrosion and fluid leaks. Test the vehicle from cold and inspect tyres, brakes, electrics, water equipment and signs of damp. A WOF is a safety check, not a full mechanical inspection. Ask an independent mechanic to assess the vehicle before purchase.

items.q: How do I sell my campervan in New Zealand?
items.a: Create a standard owner listing, add clear photos and accurate vehicle details, set the asking price, and state known defects and availability. Buyers can contact you directly. Standard owner listings are free with no sales commission; optional paid promotion is separate.

items.q: What is the best website to sell my campervan in New Zealand?
items.a: Compare platforms by listing fees, the audience and how buyers contact you. Kiwi Van Market offers free campervan listings without commission on the sale. Include accurate vehicle information, clear photos and a realistic asking price; no platform can guarantee a buyer or a sale date.

items.q: How do I sell my campervan fast before leaving New Zealand?
items.a: Start advertising before your departure date, compare similar asking prices and publish clear photos, maintenance history, WOF and rego dates and known defects. State the handover city and availability. Reply promptly and allow time for inspections. Keep a backup plan if the van does not sell in time.

items.q: How long does it take to sell a van in New Zealand?
items.a: Selling time depends on demand, season, location, asking price, vehicle condition and buyer availability. Kiwi Van Market does not publish verified sale-time statistics, so a typical number of weeks cannot be guaranteed. Leave time before departure and review your asking price and advert if enquiries are limited.

items.q: What is a buy-back guarantee for a van in NZ?
items.a: A buyback is an agreement with a particular seller, not a guarantee from Kiwi Van Market. Check who will buy, the agreed date, price, mileage and condition requirements, deductions and payment terms. An advert badge or resale calculator alone is not a binding buyback offer.

items.q: What price should I sell my van for in NZ?
items.a: Compare similar vans currently advertised by model, age, mileage, city and conversion condition. Adjust your asking price for documented maintenance, defects and upcoming costs. Advertised prices are not evidence of completed sale prices; an independent assessment can help with an unusual or expensive vehicle.

items.q: What is freedom camping in New Zealand?
items.a: Freedom camping is camping outside a campground in places covered by the relevant rules. It is permitted only where the land manager or council allows it. Check signs and official council or DOC information for each location; a self-contained certificate does not override a prohibition.

items.q: Where can I freedom camp in New Zealand?
items.a: Use council websites and DOC’s official camping information to check the exact location, restrictions, maximum stay and vehicle requirements. Travel apps can help find options, but signs and the current land-manager rules take priority. DOC campsites can have booking requirements or fees.

items.q: Do I need a self-contained certificate to freedom camp in NZ?
items.a: Vehicle requirements depend on the site and its land manager. Where certified self-contained vehicles are required, check a valid green warrant and the vehicle’s certificate; the transition ended on 7 June 2026. Some designated sites permit other vehicles. Confirm the rule for each place before staying.

items.q: What is Kiwi Van Market?
items.a: Kiwi Van Market (kiwivanmarket.com) is a marketplace connecting people buying and selling vans, campervans and motorhomes in New Zealand. Browse listings by city and model, compare seller-provided information and contact the owner directly. It is not a vehicle inspection service or a guarantee of condition.

items.q: Is Kiwi Van Market free to use?
items.a: Browsing, contacting sellers and standard owner listings are free, with no commission on the vehicle sale. Optional paid promotion is available separately; check its displayed price before purchasing.

items.q: How is Kiwi Van Market different from Trade Me?
items.a: Kiwi Van Market focuses on vans and campervans for travellers in New Zealand. Listings show seller-provided vehicle and equipment details, with free listing and no commission on the sale. Trade Me is a broader marketplace; check its current vehicle-specific terms and fees directly rather than relying on a general marketplace fee.

valueProps.title: Free listing, zero commission
valueProps.text: Listing a van on Kiwi Van Market is free, without commission on the sale. You agree the price and handover directly with the buyer.

valueProps.title: The right audience, not a general marketplace
valueProps.text: Kiwi Van Market lists campervans, vans and motorhomes only. Every visitor is looking for exactly what you are selling: backpackers and travellers buying a vehicle for their New Zealand road trip.

valueProps.title: Trust signals shown upfront
valueProps.text: Your listing displays WOF and REGO expiry dates, self-contained certification, mileage and equipment. Buyers get the answers they would otherwise have to ask for, so you receive fewer time-wasting messages.

valueProps.title: Buyers contact you directly
valueProps.text: Interested buyers reach you through in-app messages or WhatsApp. No intermediary, no lead fees — you negotiate and close the sale yourself.

valueProps.title: Optional buy-back offer
valueProps.text: You can add a buy-back guarantee to your listing: you agree to repurchase the van at a set price once the buyer trip ends. It is a strong selling point for backpackers on a fixed timeline.

valueProps.title: Multi-currency for international buyers
valueProps.text: Prices are shown in NZD, EUR, USD, AUD and GBP so overseas backpackers can judge your asking price instantly.

buyback.seoTitle: Campervan Ownership Cost Calculator NZ: Buy vs Rent
buyback.seoDesc: Compare campervan ownership and rental costs in New Zealand using your purchase price, resale assumption, expenses and rental quote. Transparent NZD scenario calculator.
buyback.intro: Start with your purchase price, assumed resale and travel days. Add costs or a rental quote when you’re ready.
buyback.explainer: Ownership cost is the purchase price minus your assumed resale proceeds, plus the expenses you enter. Divide that total by the number of travel days. Compare it with a rental quote covering the same days and comparable inclusions. Every result changes with your inputs.
buyback.factorsTitle: How to build a useful comparison

factors.name: Purchase and resale
factors.text: Use the actual purchase price and a resale assumption you can afford to miss. Compare similar advertised vans, then test a lower resale amount. Advertised prices are not evidence of completed sales.

factors.name: Inspection, repairs and servicing
factors.text: Enter your inspection quote, work identified in the report, servicing and a contingency. Leaving a field blank means zero in the arithmetic; it does not mean the cost is unnecessary.

factors.name: Insurance and administration
factors.text: Get quotes for your licence, age, trip and conversion. Add applicable licensing, RUC and selling costs to the administration budget. Use current charges for the actual vehicle.

factors.name: Rental quote
factors.text: Enter a quote for the same travel dates and length. Put additional cover, fees and equipment you need in rental extras if they are not included in the daily rate.

factors.name: Comparable running costs
factors.text: Fuel, campsites and ferries are excluded unless you include them in your entered budgets. Compare the same itinerary and cost categories on both sides; a lower ownership subtotal is not a complete trip budget.

factors.name: Actual buyback arrangements
factors.text: A seller buyback is a separate agreement. Check the named buyer, timing, amount, deductions, mileage and condition requirements, and payment terms. The calculator does not cap your trip cost or guarantee that agreement will be fulfilled.

faqs.q: Does this calculator estimate the market resale value of my campervan?
faqs.a: No. You supply the resale assumption. The tool performs transparent arithmetic on your inputs and uses no validated depreciation, brand reliability or seasonal pricing model.

faqs.q: Is buying a campervan cheaper than renting in New Zealand?
faqs.a: It depends on the purchase, eventual sale, repairs, insurance, rental quote and length of travel. Enter comparable quotes, test a lower resale amount and allow for unexpected repairs and time needed to sell.

faqs.q: What happens if my resale assumption is wrong?
faqs.a: A lower sale amount raises your ownership cost dollar for dollar. Try several resale and repair scenarios and keep enough cash available before relying on future sale proceeds.

ui.example: Illustrative example: the prefilled numbers are assumptions, not market prices or provider quotes. Replace every amount with your own budget. All entries and results are in NZD.
ui.exampleShort: Prefilled example, not market prices. Edit the amounts; all values are in NZD.
ui.resaleHint: Your assumption, not a market valuation
ui.resultNote: Resale is an assumption. Travel costs you have not entered are excluded.
ui.expensesNote: Blank expense fields count as zero. Include known costs and a contingency; check which items your quotes already cover.
ui.rentalNote: Leave the rental daily rate blank to show ownership costs only. Use the same travel days and comparable inclusions.
ui.cashRequired: Purchase plus entered expenses, before resale
ui.rentalTotal: Rental total for the same days
ui.buyLower: With these inputs, the ownership subtotal is lower. Future sale proceeds and costs remain uncertain.
ui.rentLower: With these inputs, the rental subtotal is lower.
ui.equal: The two subtotals are equal with these inputs.
ui.formula: Ownership = purchase − assumed resale + inspection + repairs + insurance + administration. Rental = days × quoted daily rate + rental extras.
ui.invalid: Enter a positive purchase price and number of days, an assumed resale amount of zero or more, and non-negative costs.
ui.limits: This scenario excludes costs you have not entered. Cash needed before resale and final trip cost are different: future sale proceeds are not available to fund the purchase.
